title: Find all employees who share the same birthday month.
shortTitle: Find all employees who share the same birthday month

s1_definition.profdef: You group employees by their birth month, then keep only the groups with more than one member, revealing months in which multiple employees share a birthday month.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya sorts employees into month bins by birthday and keeps only the bins that have two or more people.
s1_definition.oneliner: `groupingBy(dob.getMonth())`, then keep entries with more than one employee.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** You group employees by their birth month, then keep only the groups with more than one member, revealing months in which multiple employees share a birthday month.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Priya sorts employees into month bins by birthday and keeps only the bins that have two or more people.

**One line to remember:** `groupingBy(dob.getMonth())`, then keep entries with more than one employee.

sections.s2_technical:
`groupingBy(e -> e.getDob().getMonth(), mapping(Employee::getName, toList()))` buckets employees by their birth Month enum and keeps the names per month. You then filter the map's entries to those whose list has size greater than one, giving the months where employees share a birthday month and who they are.

The result is a `Map<Month, List<String>>` restricted to shared months. Grouping by the Month enum is clean and type-safe. The size-greater-than-one filter is the same "appears more than once" pattern applied at the group level.

The senior nuance is whether the requirement is the same month or the same exact day — I group by Month for "same month" and would group by MonthDay for "same day". I guard null dates of birth, decide whether to keep singletons out, and the Month enum avoids locale issues. Filtering groups by their size is a clean way to find any "shared attribute" relationship.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — An events team at the National Bank of India plans combined monthly birthday celebrations and needs the months where multiple employees share a birthday month.

This is exactly what group-by-month then keep-size-over-one does — it surfaces the shared months and their people.

The code defines a `BirthdayGroupService.sharedBirthdayMonths method and a demo.
sections.s5_journey:
Input: Rajesh June, Amit June, Priya March.

Step 1: grouping by month buckets Rajesh and Amit under JUNE and Priya under MARCH.

Step 2: The size filter keeps months with more than one employee.

Step 3: JUNE has two names and survives; MARCH has one and is dropped.

Step 4: The result maps JUNE to Rajesh and Amit.

```
INFO: JUNE → [Rajesh, Amit]
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  [Rajesh/June, Amit/June, Priya/March]
    │ groupingBy(dob.getMonth(), mapping(name))
    │ → {JUNE=[Rajesh, Amit], MARCH=[Priya]}
    │ filter(group size > 1)
    ▼
  {JUNE=[Rajesh, Amit]}
```

sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — shared-attribute via group size ═══

  ┌─ group then filter by size ────────────────────────────────┐
  │ groupingBy(dob.getMonth(), mapping(name, toList))          │
  │ filter(entry.value.size() > 1) → months with 2+ people     │
  │ Month enum → type-safe, no locale issues                   │
  │ same-DAY instead → group by MonthDay                       │
  │ guard null dob; "shared" = group size > 1                  │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
  │        BirthdayGroupService   │
  │  + sharedBirthdayMonths(List)   │ group(month)→filter size>1
  └───────────────────────────────┘

  Call chain:
  1. groupingBy(getMonth, mapping(name, toList))
  2. entrySet().filter(size > 1)
  3. toMap → shared months
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
To find employees who share a birthday month I group them by the month of their date of birth, keeping the names per month, and then filter the resulting map to the entries whose list has more than one member. That leaves exactly the months in which two or more employees share a birthday month, along with who they are. At the National Bank of India this backs an events team planning combined monthly birthday celebrations.

I group by the Month enum, which is type-safe and free of locale issues, and I guard against null dates of birth before extracting the month. The size-greater-than-one filter is the group-level version of the "appears more than once" pattern — instead of duplicate values, I am finding groups that contain multiple members.

The senior point I stress is being precise about the requirement: same month means grouping by Month, whereas same exact day would mean grouping by MonthDay, and I confirm which the business wants. Filtering groups by their size is a clean, general way to express any "shared attribute" relationship — shared month, shared city, shared manager — by grouping on the attribute and keeping the groups larger than one.
